# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24
    secrets:
      APP_ID:
        description: 'Optional GitHub App id (awf#52). With APP_PRIVATE_KEY set, guard API calls ride a per-job App installation token instead of github.token. Absent => github.token, byte-identical to today.'
        required: false
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY:
        description: 'Private key (PEM) of the APP_ID GitHub App.'
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The CALLER repository, pinned to the SAME frozen identity
          # PUSHED_SHA uses (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha):
          # the tree under assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD,
          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL \
            "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/main/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py"

      # GitHub App auth (awf#52): with APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets the
      # guard's gh calls ride a per-job App installation token; absent them
      # github.token is used, byte-identical to today.
      - name: Resolve GitHub auth (App -> github.token)
        id: app
        env:
          APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$APP_ID" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: app"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: pat"
          fi

      - name: Mint GitHub App installation token
        id: app-token
        if: steps.app.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow }}
          WINDOW_HOURS: ${{ inputs.window_hours }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can
          # drift to a main that moved in the seconds before the job
          # starts (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag
          # BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --workflow "$CI_WORKFLOW" \
            --window-hours "$WINDOW_HOURS" \
            --alarm-issue

# gh-1044: [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)

## Description

## Live evidence (2026-10-18)

Alarm gh-1033 fired on the merge of PR #1020 (main commit `d10dbcba03a1`):

> Guard verdict: no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree

**The tree WAS validated green.** PR #1020 merged head `32f43df1` (tree `89755209ac7d` = the squashed main commit tree — main had not moved). Quality run https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39126212895 covered exactly that head — **success** — but with `event: pull_request` (branch push by the conflict-rework leg → PR synchronize → Quality), not `workflow_dispatch`.

## Root cause

The guard's tree-coverage probe (gh-1537 AC5) considers only `workflow_dispatch`-event quality.yml runs. In this repo most validations arrive as `pull_request`-event runs (legs push to the PR branch, CI fires on synchronize). The merge side correctly accepted the green pull_request run (merge-validated consumed it) — the guard disagreed, so a clean, validated merge reads as "SM merged without validation".

## Fix

The guard must count a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`, `pull_request`, `push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree — or at minimum add `pull_request`. The check is about *tree coverage by a green validation*, not about *who dispatched it*.

## Why not just silence the alarm

A too-narrow coverage check cries wolf on every conflict-rework merge (legs push → pull_request CI → merge): operators learn to ignore `[sm-guard]` alarms, and the one real unvalidated merge drowns in false positives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the gh-1033 inputs (merged tree `89755209ac7d`, green pull_request run 39126212895 on head 32f43df1) yields NO alarm.
- [ ] A merge whose tree has NO green run of any event still alarms (true positive preserved).
- [ ] Unit test: coverage probe accepts pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch green runs alike; rejects red/in-flight runs of any event.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SM merge guard (gh-1537 AC5) — the cheap alarm for the serialized-
validation invariant.

Invariant under watch: the SM queue (machine-sm.yml -> factory-sm) is
strictly serialized and validates the EXACT tree that merges — update
branch onto main, dispatch ci.yml on the updated head, merge only when
green. With the post-merge main CI run retired (gh-1537), nothing else
stands between a violated invariant and a red main: this guard fires on
every push to main and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a
SUCCESSFUL ci.yml workflow_dispatch run (an SM pre-merge validation).

A push whose tree has no successful dispatched validation is the
#687-invariant violation the owner asked to alarm on instead of relying
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard —
defense-in-depth: gh-1522 retired the bump flow so none land anymore, but
if one ever returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the full
quality gate that runs on the cut v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

ALARM_LABEL = "sm-guard"
# Cap the per-run tree lookups: validations are fresh (minutes before the
# merge), so the matching run is always among the most recent dispatches;
# the cap bounds gh api calls per push, not correctness.
MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS = 40


def gh(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"gh {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
    return proc.stdout


def fetch_validated_runs(repo: str, workflow: str,
                         window_hours: int) -> list:
    """Recent SUCCESSFUL <workflow> workflow_dispatch runs, each with the
    tree sha of its head commit resolved via the commits API."""
    since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=window_hours)
    out = gh("run", "list", "--repo", repo, "--workflow", workflow,
             "--event", "workflow_dispatch",
             "--json", "databaseId,headSha,conclusion,createdAt",
             "--limit", "100")
    runs = []
    for r in json.loads(out):
        if r.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        created = datetime.fromisoformat(
            r["createdAt"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if created < since:
            continue
        runs.append({
            "database_id": r["databaseId"],
            "head_sha": r["headSha"],
            # decide() re-checks conclusion on every run; without the
            # field every fetched run read as None != "success" and was
            # skipped — the guard alarmed on every push (gh-1568).
            "conclusion": r.get("conclusion"),
            "tree_sha": None,  # resolved below
            "created_at": r["createdAt"],
        })
    # Newest first — the match is almost always the first lookup.
    for run in runs[:MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS]:
        try:
            # The commits API nests the tree under `commit` — `.tree.sha`
            # resolves to null/empty (gh-1568: every tree match silently
            # failed and every merge-commit landing false-alarmed).
            tree = gh("api", f"repos/{repo}/commits/{run['head_sha']}",
                      "--jq", ".commit.tree.sha").strip()
            run["tree_sha"] = tree or None
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"::warning::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
    return runs


def decide(subject: str, pushed_sha: str, pushed_tree: str,
           runs: list, workflow: str = "ci.yml") -> dict:
    """The pure invariant check. `runs` carry head_sha/tree_sha of
    successful dispatched validations. Returns a verdict dict."""
    if subject.startswith("chore(release):"):
        return {"verdict": "skipped",
                "reason": "release-bot bump push — the v* tag run gates it"}
    for run in runs:
        # Only successes validate — a run with NO conclusion was never
        # confirmed green, so it can never certify a push
        # (fetch_validated_runs pre-filters, but the test seam and any
        # future caller may pass mixed or incomplete run dicts — the
        # invariant holds by construction).
        if run.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        if run.get("head_sha") == pushed_sha:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"exact head-SHA match: run "
                              f"{run.get('database_id')} validated the "
                              f"merged commit itself (fast-forward)"}
        if run.get("tree_sha") and run["tree_sha"] == pushed_tree:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"tree match: run {run.get('database_id')} "
                              f"validated this exact tree (squash/merge "
                              f"commit re-landed it)"}
    return {"verdict": "alarm",
            "reason": f"no successful {workflow} workflow_dispatch run "
                      f"covers this tree — the SM merged without (or "
                      f"before) a green validation of the exact tree"}


def alarm_issue(repo: str, pushed_sha: str, subject: str, reason: str,
                runs: list) -> None:
    """File or update the deduplicated sm-guard issue (ci-red-report
    convention: one open issue per guard, comments for repeats)."""
    links = "\n".join(
        f"- https://github.com/{repo}/actions/runs/{r.get('database_id')}"
        f" (head `{r.get('head_sha')}`"
        + (f", tree `{r['tree_sha']}`" if r.get("tree_sha") else "")
        + ")"
        for r in runs[:10])
    # An empty commit message (git commit --allow-empty-message / the Git
    # API) would crash the alarm itself on splitlines()[0] — the one path
    # where the sm-guard issue would be lost for exactly the push that
    # tripped it. Degrade to a placeholder instead.
    subject_line = (subject.splitlines()[0]
                    if subject.splitlines() else "(empty commit message)")
    body = (
        f"**Pushed SHA**: `{pushed_sha}`\n"
        f"**Subject**: {subject_line}\n\n"
        f"**Why this is an alarm** (gh-1537 AC5): the SM queue must be "
        f"strictly serialized and validate the exact tree that merges. "
        f"This push to main has no successful ci.yml validation dispatch "
        f"covering its tree.\n\n"
        f"**Guard verdict**: {reason}\n\n"
        f"Recent dispatched validation runs considered:\n"
        f"{links or '(none in the window)'}\n")
    existing = gh("issue", "list", "--repo", repo, "--state", "open",
                  "--label", ALARM_LABEL,
                  "--json", "number", "--jq", ".[0].number // empty")
    if existing.strip():
        gh("issue", "comment", existing.strip(), "--repo", repo,
           "--body", body)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: commented on #{existing.strip()}")
    else:
        out = gh("issue", "create", "--repo", repo,
                 "--title", f"[sm-guard] main push without validated tree: "
                            f"{pushed_sha[:12]}",
                 "--body", body, "--label", "bug", "--label", ALARM_LABEL)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: filed {out.strip().splitlines()[-1]}")

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

blocks.text:
# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24
    secrets:
      APP_ID:
        description: 'Optional GitHub App id (awf#52). With APP_PRIVATE_KEY set, guard API calls ride a per-job App installation token instead of github.token. Absent => github.token, byte-identical to today.'
        required: false
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY:
        description: 'Private key (PEM) of the APP_ID GitHub App.'
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The CALLER repository, pinned to the SAME frozen identity
          # PUSHED_SHA uses (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha):
          # the tree under assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD,
          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL \
            "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/main/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py"

      # GitHub App auth (awf#52): with APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets the
      # guard's gh calls ride a per-job App installation token; absent them
      # github.token is used, byte-identical to today.
      - name: Resolve GitHub auth (App -> github.token)
        id: app
        env:
          APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$APP_ID" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: app"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: pat"
          fi

      - name: Mint GitHub App installation token
        id: app-token
        if: steps.app.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow }}
          WINDOW_HOURS: ${{ inputs.window_hours }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can
          # drift to a main that moved in the seconds before the job
          # starts (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag
          # BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --workflow "$CI_WORKFLOW" \
            --window-hours "$WINDOW_HOURS" \
            --alarm-issue

# gh-1044: [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)

## Description

## Live evidence (2026-10-18)

Alarm gh-1033 fired on the merge of PR #1020 (main commit `d10dbcba03a1`):

> Guard verdict: no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree

**The tree WAS validated green.** PR #1020 merged head `32f43df1` (tree `89755209ac7d` = the squashed main commit tree — main had not moved). Quality run https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39126212895 covered exactly that head — **success** — but with `event: pull_request` (branch push by the conflict-rework leg → PR synchronize → Quality), not `workflow_dispatch`.

## Root cause

The guard's tree-coverage probe (gh-1537 AC5) considers only `workflow_dispatch`-event quality.yml runs. In this repo most validations arrive as `pull_request`-event runs (legs push to the PR branch, CI fires on synchronize). The merge side correctly accepted the green pull_request run (merge-validated consumed it) — the guard disagreed, so a clean, validated merge reads as "SM merged without validation".

## Fix

The guard must count a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`, `pull_request`, `push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree — or at minimum add `pull_request`. The check is about *tree coverage by a green validation*, not about *who dispatched it*.

## Why not just silence the alarm

A too-narrow coverage check cries wolf on every conflict-rework merge (legs push → pull_request CI → merge): operators learn to ignore `[sm-guard]` alarms, and the one real unvalidated merge drowns in false positives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the gh-1033 inputs (merged tree `89755209ac7d`, green pull_request run 39126212895 on head 32f43df1) yields NO alarm.
- [ ] A merge whose tree has NO green run of any event still alarms (true positive preserved).
- [ ] Unit test: coverage probe accepts pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch green runs alike; rejects red/in-flight runs of any event.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SM merge guard (gh-1537 AC5) — the cheap alarm for the serialized-
validation invariant.

Invariant under watch: the SM queue (machine-sm.yml -> factory-sm) is
strictly serialized and validates the EXACT tree that merges — update
branch onto main, dispatch ci.yml on the updated head, merge only when
green. With the post-merge main CI run retired (gh-1537), nothing else
stands between a violated invariant and a red main: this guard fires on
every push to main and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a
SUCCESSFUL ci.yml workflow_dispatch run (an SM pre-merge validation).

A push whose tree has no successful dispatched validation is the
#687-invariant violation the owner asked to alarm on instead of relying
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard —
defense-in-depth: gh-1522 retired the bump flow so none land anymore, but
if one ever returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the full
quality gate that runs on the cut v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

ALARM_LABEL = "sm-guard"
# Cap the per-run tree lookups: validations are fresh (minutes before the
# merge), so the matching run is always among the most recent dispatches;
# the cap bounds gh api calls per push, not correctness.
MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS = 40


def gh(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"gh {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
    return proc.stdout


def fetch_validated_runs(repo: str, workflow: str,
                         window_hours: int) -> list:
    """Recent SUCCESSFUL <workflow> workflow_dispatch runs, each with the
    tree sha of its head commit resolved via the commits API."""
    since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=window_hours)
    out = gh("run", "list", "--repo", repo, "--workflow", workflow,
             "--event", "workflow_dispatch",
             "--json", "databaseId,headSha,conclusion,createdAt",
             "--limit", "100")
    runs = []
    for r in json.loads(out):
        if r.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        created = datetime.fromisoformat(
            r["createdAt"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if created < since:
            continue
        runs.append({
            "database_id": r["databaseId"],
            "head_sha": r["headSha"],
            # decide() re-checks conclusion on every run; without the
            # field every fetched run read as None != "success" and was
            # skipped — the guard alarmed on every push (gh-1568).
            "conclusion": r.get("conclusion"),
            "tree_sha": None,  # resolved below
            "created_at": r["createdAt"],
        })
    # Newest first — the match is almost always the first lookup.
    for run in runs[:MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS]:
        try:
            # The commits API nests the tree under `commit` — `.tree.sha`
            # resolves to null/empty (gh-1568: every tree match silently
            # failed and every merge-commit landing false-alarmed).
            tree = gh("api", f"repos/{repo}/commits/{run['head_sha']}",
                      "--jq", ".commit.tree.sha").strip()
            run["tree_sha"] = tree or None
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"::warning::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
    return runs


def decide(subject: str, pushed_sha: str, pushed_tree: str,
           runs: list, workflow: str = "ci.yml") -> dict:
    """The pure invariant check. `runs` carry head_sha/tree_sha of
    successful dispatched validations. Returns a verdict dict."""
    if subject.startswith("chore(release):"):
        return {"verdict": "skipped",
                "reason": "release-bot bump push — the v* tag run gates it"}
    for run in runs:
        # Only successes validate — a run with NO conclusion was never
        # confirmed green, so it can never certify a push
        # (fetch_validated_runs pre-filters, but the test seam and any
        # future caller may pass mixed or incomplete run dicts — the
        # invariant holds by construction).
        if run.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        if run.get("head_sha") == pushed_sha:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"exact head-SHA match: run "
                              f"{run.get('database_id')} validated the "
                              f"merged commit itself (fast-forward)"}
        if run.get("tree_sha") and run["tree_sha"] == pushed_tree:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"tree match: run {run.get('database_id')} "
                              f"validated this exact tree (squash/merge "
                              f"commit re-landed it)"}
    return {"verdict": "alarm",
            "reason": f"no successful {workflow} workflow_dispatch run "
                      f"covers this tree — the SM merged without (or "
                      f"before) a green validation of the exact tree"}


def alarm_issue(repo: str, pushed_sha: str, subject: str, reason: str,
                runs: list) -> None:
    """File or update the deduplicated sm-guard issue (ci-red-report
    convention: one open issue per guard, comments for repeats)."""
    links = "\n".join(
        f"- https://github.com/{repo}/actions/runs/{r.get('database_id')}"
        f" (head `{r.get('head_sha')}`"
        + (f", tree `{r['tree_sha']}`" if r.get("tree_sha") else "")
        + ")"
        for r in runs[:10])
    # An empty commit message (git commit --allow-empty-message / the Git
    # API) would crash the alarm itself on splitlines()[0] — the one path
    # where the sm-guard issue would be lost for exactly the push that
    # tripped it. Degrade to a placeholder instead.
    subject_line = (subject.splitlines()[0]
                    if subject.splitlines() else "(empty commit message)")
    body = (
        f"**Pushed SHA**: `{pushed_sha}`\n"
        f"**Subject**: {subject_line}\n\n"
        f"**Why this is an alarm** (gh-1537 AC5): the SM queue must be "
        f"strictly serialized and validate the exact tree that merges. "
        f"This push to main has no successful ci.yml validation dispatch "
        f"covering its tree.\n\n"
        f"**Guard verdict**: {reason}\n\n"
        f"Recent dispatched validation runs considered:\n"
        f"{links or '(none in the window)'}\n")
    existing = gh("issue", "list", "--repo", repo, "--state", "open",
                  "--label", ALARM_LABEL,
                  "--json", "number", "--jq", ".[0].number // empty")
    if existing.strip():
        gh("issue", "comment", existing.strip(), "--repo", repo,
           "--body", body)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: commented on #{existing.strip()}")
    else:
        out = gh("issue", "create", "--repo", repo,
                 "--title", f"[sm-guard] main push without validated tree: "
                            f"{pushed_sha[:12]}",
                 "--body", body, "--label", "bug", "--label", ALARM_LABEL)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: filed {out.strip().splitlines()[-1]}")

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring

blocks.text:
# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24
    secrets:
      APP_ID:
        description: 'Optional GitHub App id (awf#52). With APP_PRIVATE_KEY set, guard API calls ride a per-job App installation token instead of github.token. Absent => github.token, byte-identical to today.'
        required: false
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY:
        description: 'Private key (PEM) of the APP_ID GitHub App.'
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The CALLER repository, pinned to the SAME frozen identity
          # PUSHED_SHA uses (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha):
          # the tree under assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD,
          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL \
            "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/main/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py"

      # GitHub App auth (awf#52): with APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets the
      # guard's gh calls ride a per-job App installation token; absent them
      # github.token is used, byte-identical to today.
      - name: Resolve GitHub auth (App -> github.token)
        id: app
        env:
          APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$APP_ID" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: app"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: pat"
          fi

      - name: Mint GitHub App installation token
        id: app-token
        if: steps.app.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow }}
          WINDOW_HOURS: ${{ inputs.window_hours }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can
          # drift to a main that moved in the seconds before the job
          # starts (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag
          # BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --workflow "$CI_WORKFLOW" \
            --window-hours "$WINDOW_HOURS" \
            --alarm-issue

# gh-1044: [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)

## Description

## Live evidence (2026-10-18)

Alarm gh-1033 fired on the merge of PR #1020 (main commit `d10dbcba03a1`):

> Guard verdict: no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree

**The tree WAS validated green.** PR #1020 merged head `32f43df1` (tree `89755209ac7d` = the squashed main commit tree — main had not moved). Quality run https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39126212895 covered exactly that head — **success** — but with `event: pull_request` (branch push by the conflict-rework leg → PR synchronize → Quality), not `workflow_dispatch`.

## Root cause

The guard's tree-coverage probe (gh-1537 AC5) considers only `workflow_dispatch`-event quality.yml runs. In this repo most validations arrive as `pull_request`-event runs (legs push to the PR branch, CI fires on synchronize). The merge side correctly accepted the green pull_request run (merge-validated consumed it) — the guard disagreed, so a clean, validated merge reads as "SM merged without validation".

## Fix

The guard must count a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`, `pull_request`, `push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree — or at minimum add `pull_request`. The check is about *tree coverage by a green validation*, not about *who dispatched it*.

## Why not just silence the alarm

A too-narrow coverage check cries wolf on every conflict-rework merge (legs push → pull_request CI → merge): operators learn to ignore `[sm-guard]` alarms, and the one real unvalidated merge drowns in false positives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the gh-1033 inputs (merged tree `89755209ac7d`, green pull_request run 39126212895 on head 32f43df1) yields NO alarm.
- [ ] A merge whose tree has NO green run of any event still alarms (true positive preserved).
- [ ] Unit test: coverage probe accepts pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch green runs alike; rejects red/in-flight runs of any event.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""SM merge guard (gh-1537 AC5) — the cheap alarm for the serialized-
validation invariant.

Invariant under watch: the SM queue (machine-sm.yml -> factory-sm) is
strictly serialized and validates the EXACT tree that merges — update
branch onto main, dispatch ci.yml on the updated head, merge only when
green. With the post-merge main CI run retired (gh-1537), nothing else
stands between a violated invariant and a red main: this guard fires on
every push to main and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a
SUCCESSFUL ci.yml workflow_dispatch run (an SM pre-merge validation).

A push whose tree has no successful dispatched validation is the
#687-invariant violation the owner asked to alarm on instead of relying
on a nightly backstop: the guard files/updates one `sm-guard`-labelled
issue (dedup by comment, same convention as ci-red-report).

Match semantics: TREE identity, not commit identity — the SM may land a
merge as a fast-forward (same commit SHA as the validated head) or as a
squash/merge commit (new SHA, byte-identical tree). The ticket's
invariant is literally "the tree that lands in main is byte-identical to
the validated tree", so `git rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` of the push is
compared against the tree of each recent successful dispatch run's head
(with an exact head-SHA match accepted as the fast-forward case).

Release-bot bump pushes (`chore(release):` subjects) skip the guard —
defense-in-depth: gh-1522 retired the bump flow so none land anymore, but
if one ever returns it is release-flow, gated downstream by the full
quality gate that runs on the cut v* tag BEFORE publish/binaries.

Exit codes: 0 = validated / skipped, 3 = invariant violated (alarm filed
when --alarm-issue), 1 = gh/tooling error, 2 = usage error.

Pure stdlib + gh. The decision itself (`decide`) takes pre-fetched runs
so the unit test injects fixtures via --runs-json — no network, no gh.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

ALARM_LABEL = "sm-guard"
# Cap the per-run tree lookups: validations are fresh (minutes before the
# merge), so the matching run is always among the most recent dispatches;
# the cap bounds gh api calls per push, not correctness.
MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS = 40


def gh(*args: str, check: bool = True) -> str:
    proc = subprocess.run(["gh", *args], capture_output=True, text=True)
    if check and proc.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"gh {' '.join(args)} failed: {proc.stderr.strip()}")
    return proc.stdout


def fetch_validated_runs(repo: str, workflow: str,
                         window_hours: int) -> list:
    """Recent SUCCESSFUL <workflow> workflow_dispatch runs, each with the
    tree sha of its head commit resolved via the commits API."""
    since = datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=window_hours)
    out = gh("run", "list", "--repo", repo, "--workflow", workflow,
             "--event", "workflow_dispatch",
             "--json", "databaseId,headSha,conclusion,createdAt",
             "--limit", "100")
    runs = []
    for r in json.loads(out):
        if r.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        created = datetime.fromisoformat(
            r["createdAt"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if created < since:
            continue
        runs.append({
            "database_id": r["databaseId"],
            "head_sha": r["headSha"],
            # decide() re-checks conclusion on every run; without the
            # field every fetched run read as None != "success" and was
            # skipped — the guard alarmed on every push (gh-1568).
            "conclusion": r.get("conclusion"),
            "tree_sha": None,  # resolved below
            "created_at": r["createdAt"],
        })
    # Newest first — the match is almost always the first lookup.
    for run in runs[:MAX_TREE_LOOKUPS]:
        try:
            # The commits API nests the tree under `commit` — `.tree.sha`
            # resolves to null/empty (gh-1568: every tree match silently
            # failed and every merge-commit landing false-alarmed).
            tree = gh("api", f"repos/{repo}/commits/{run['head_sha']}",
                      "--jq", ".commit.tree.sha").strip()
            run["tree_sha"] = tree or None
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"::warning::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
    return runs


def decide(subject: str, pushed_sha: str, pushed_tree: str,
           runs: list, workflow: str = "ci.yml") -> dict:
    """The pure invariant check. `runs` carry head_sha/tree_sha of
    successful dispatched validations. Returns a verdict dict."""
    if subject.startswith("chore(release):"):
        return {"verdict": "skipped",
                "reason": "release-bot bump push — the v* tag run gates it"}
    for run in runs:
        # Only successes validate — a run with NO conclusion was never
        # confirmed green, so it can never certify a push
        # (fetch_validated_runs pre-filters, but the test seam and any
        # future caller may pass mixed or incomplete run dicts — the
        # invariant holds by construction).
        if run.get("conclusion") != "success":
            continue
        if run.get("head_sha") == pushed_sha:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"exact head-SHA match: run "
                              f"{run.get('database_id')} validated the "
                              f"merged commit itself (fast-forward)"}
        if run.get("tree_sha") and run["tree_sha"] == pushed_tree:
            return {"verdict": "ok",
                    "reason": f"tree match: run {run.get('database_id')} "
                              f"validated this exact tree (squash/merge "
                              f"commit re-landed it)"}
    return {"verdict": "alarm",
            "reason": f"no successful {workflow} workflow_dispatch run "
                      f"covers this tree — the SM merged without (or "
                      f"before) a green validation of the exact tree"}


def alarm_issue(repo: str, pushed_sha: str, subject: str, reason: str,
                runs: list) -> None:
    """File or update the deduplicated sm-guard issue (ci-red-report
    convention: one open issue per guard, comments for repeats)."""
    links = "\n".join(
        f"- https://github.com/{repo}/actions/runs/{r.get('database_id')}"
        f" (head `{r.get('head_sha')}`"
        + (f", tree `{r['tree_sha']}`" if r.get("tree_sha") else "")
        + ")"
        for r in runs[:10])
    # An empty commit message (git commit --allow-empty-message / the Git
    # API) would crash the alarm itself on splitlines()[0] — the one path
    # where the sm-guard issue would be lost for exactly the push that
    # tripped it. Degrade to a placeholder instead.
    subject_line = (subject.splitlines()[0]
                    if subject.splitlines() else "(empty commit message)")
    body = (
        f"**Pushed SHA**: `{pushed_sha}`\n"
        f"**Subject**: {subject_line}\n\n"
        f"**Why this is an alarm** (gh-1537 AC5): the SM queue must be "
        f"strictly serialized and validate the exact tree that merges. "
        f"This push to main has no successful ci.yml validation dispatch "
        f"covering its tree.\n\n"
        f"**Guard verdict**: {reason}\n\n"
        f"Recent dispatched validation runs considered:\n"
        f"{links or '(none in the window)'}\n")
    existing = gh("issue", "list", "--repo", repo, "--state", "open",
                  "--label", ALARM_LABEL,
                  "--json", "number", "--jq", ".[0].number // empty")
    if existing.strip():
        gh("issue", "comment", existing.strip(), "--repo", repo,
           "--body", body)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: commented on #{existing.strip()}")
    else:
        out = gh("issue", "create", "--repo", repo,
                 "--title", f"[sm-guard] main push without validated tree: "
                            f"{pushed_sha[:12]}",
                 "--body", body, "--label", "bug", "--label", ALARM_LABEL)
        print(f"::warning::sm-guard: filed {out.strip().splitlines()[-1]}")

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write

# Factory SM merge guard — canonical home (reusable).
#
# The cheap alarm for the SM serialized-validation invariant (gh-1537 AC5,
# bugs fixed gh-1568): with the post-merge main CI run retired, nothing
# else stands between a violated invariant ("SM queue is strictly
# serialized and validates the exact tree being merged") and a red main.
# This workflow fires on EVERY push to main (via the caller repo's thin
# stub) and asserts the pushed tree was covered by a successful
# workflow_dispatch run of the repo's validation CI — the SM's pre-merge
# validation. A push without one files/updates one deduplicated
# `sm-guard` issue (event-driven, seconds of runner time — explicitly NOT
# a nightly/polling backstop, per the owner's directive).
#
# A `chore(release):` bump push skips the guard (defense-in-depth). SM
# merge commits and any human/admin push are checked — tree identity, so
# both fast-forward (same SHA) and squash/merge-commit (same tree)
# landings validate.
#
# Canonical home pattern (same as factory-sm-kicker.yml): the calling
# repo keeps a thin stub workflow with its own `on: push: [main]`
# trigger that calls this one with repo-specific inputs.
name: Factory SM merge guard

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ci_workflow:
        description: 'File name of the validation CI workflow the SM dispatches (ci.yml, quality.yml, ...)'
        type: string
        default: 'ci.yml'
      window_hours:
        description: 'How far back dispatched validation runs certify a push'
        type: number
        default: 24
    secrets:
      APP_ID:
        description: 'Optional GitHub App id (awf#52). With APP_PRIVATE_KEY set, guard API calls ride a per-job App installation token instead of github.token. Absent => github.token, byte-identical to today.'
        required: false
      APP_PRIVATE_KEY:
        description: 'Private key (PEM) of the APP_ID GitHub App.'
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  guard:
    name: Validate the pushed tree was SM-validated
    runs-on: ubuntu-slim
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write # the sm-guard alarm issue
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The CALLER repository, pinned to the SAME frozen identity
          # PUSHED_SHA uses (github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha):
          # the tree under assertion is read from this checkout's HEAD,
          # so an unpinned checkout could drift to a moved main and have
          # run-for-push-A certify a newer push B's tree it never examined
          # (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag BUMP_SHA pin).
          ref: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          # Only the pushed tree sha is read — no history, no blobs.
          fetch-depth: 1

      - name: Fetch the canonical guard script (factory home @ main)
        # Always-latest policy (owner 2026-10-04, kicker parity): guard
        # fixes go live on merge, no re-pin ceremony. The script is
        # hermetic (gh + python3 only), so a main ref here is the same
        # trust level as `uses: ...factory-*.yml@main` in the stubs.
        run: |
          curl -fsSL \
            "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/main/scripts/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            -o "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py"

      # GitHub App auth (awf#52): with APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets the
      # guard's gh calls ride a per-job App installation token; absent them
      # github.token is used, byte-identical to today.
      - name: Resolve GitHub auth (App -> github.token)
        id: app
        env:
          APP_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$APP_ID" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: app"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "auth: pat"
          fi

      - name: Mint GitHub App installation token
        id: app-token
        if: steps.app.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@v2
        with:
          app-id: ${{ secrets.APP_ID }}
          private-key: ${{ secrets.APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}

      - name: Assert a dispatched validation covers this tree
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token || github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          CI_WORKFLOW: ${{ inputs.ci_workflow }}
          WINDOW_HOURS: ${{ inputs.window_hours }}
          # head_commit.id is frozen at push time — the checkout can
          # drift to a main that moved in the seconds before the job
          # starts (same lesson as the retired ci.yml release-tag
          # BUMP_SHA pin, #1178).
          PUSHED_SHA: ${{ github.event.head_commit.id || github.sha }}
          PUSHED_SUBJECT: ${{ github.event.head_commit.message }}
        run: |
          tree=$(git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}')
          python3 "$RUNNER_TEMP/sm_merge_guard.py" \
            --repo "$REPO" \
            --sha "$PUSHED_SHA" \
            --subject "$PUSHED_SUBJECT" \
            --tree "$tree" \
            --workflow "$CI_WORKFLOW" \
            --window-hours "$WINDOW_HOURS" \
            --alarm-issue

content.text:
/**
 * CI check-run mirroring for dispatch-only workflows.
 *
 * Problem: when a repository's CI is triggered via workflow_dispatch
 * (no pull_request trigger), GitHub does not associate the run's check
 * runs with open PRs — the branch-protection required checks stay
 * "expected/pending" forever, and the real pass/fail is invisible in
 * the PR Checks tab (a zombie check-run may exist on the head SHA from
 * a stale push event).
 *
 * Fix: re-read the ACTUAL jobs of the dispatch run and re-create one
 * check-run per required check name on the PR head SHA (same names,
 * same conclusions, summary links back to the source run). GitHub's
 * Checks UI and branch protection take the LATEST check-run per
 * (name, head SHA), so the mirror overrides any zombie.
 *
 * Tools used (dmtools registry, snake_case, synchronous):
 *   github_get_workflow_run_jobs({workspace, repository, runId})
 *       -> { total_count, jobs: [{id, name, status, conclusion, html_url}] }
 *   github_create_check_run({workspace, repository, name, headSha
 *       [, status][, title][, summary][, text]})
 *       -> check-run object (use .id for the follow-up update)
 *   github_update_check_run({workspace, repository, checkRunId,
 *       status, conclusion[, title][, summary][, text]})
 *   github_create_commit_status({workspace, repository, sha, state
 *       [, description][, context][, targetUrl]})
 *
 * Conclusion policy (documented behaviour of stampRequiredChecks):
 *   - job.conclusion === 'skipped'         -> NOT stamped (a skipped job
 *       must never green a required check); recorded in `skipped`.
 *   - job.status !== 'completed' (running/queued/null conclusion)
 *                                          -> NOT stamped; `skipped`
 *       entry with reason 'not-completed'.
 *   - success | neutral                    -> stamped as 'success' (and
 *       commit-status 'success' when the fallback is on).
 *   - failure | timed_out | startup_failure | cancelled | action_required
 *                                          -> stamped as-is ('cancelled'
 *       and 'action_required' map to commit-status 'failure' — GitHub
 *       statuses have no neutral value, and a cancelled CI run must not
 *       read as green on a PR).
 *
 * Job matching: required check `name` is matched EXACTLY against the
 * job `name` (GitHub matrix jobs include the parenthesised variant, so
 * list the full name, e.g. "build (ubuntu-latest)"). When several jobs
 * share a name (re-runs, matrix), the LAST match in the run's job list
 * wins — it is the most recent attempt. A required entry may override
 * the matched job name with `jobName` when the protected check name
 * intentionally differs from the workflow job name.
 */

function _parseJson(raw) {
    if (typeof raw === 'string') {
        try { return JSON.parse(raw); } catch (e) { return raw; }
    }
    return raw;
}

function _jobsOf(response) {
    var parsed = _parseJson(response);
    if (parsed && Array.isArray(parsed.jobs)) return parsed.jobs;

# gh-1044: [sm-guard] false positive: pull_request-event validation runs don't count as tree coverage (live: #1020 merge, alarm gh-1033)

## Description

## Live evidence (2026-10-18)

Alarm gh-1033 fired on the merge of PR #1020 (main commit `d10dbcba03a1`):

> Guard verdict: no successful quality.yml workflow_dispatch run covers this tree

**The tree WAS validated green.** PR #1020 merged head `32f43df1` (tree `89755209ac7d` = the squashed main commit tree — main had not moved). Quality run https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/actions/runs/39126212895 covered exactly that head — **success** — but with `event: pull_request` (branch push by the conflict-rework leg → PR synchronize → Quality), not `workflow_dispatch`.

## Root cause

The guard's tree-coverage probe (gh-1537 AC5) considers only `workflow_dispatch`-event quality.yml runs. In this repo most validations arrive as `pull_request`-event runs (legs push to the PR branch, CI fires on synchronize). The merge side correctly accepted the green pull_request run (merge-validated consumed it) — the guard disagreed, so a clean, validated merge reads as "SM merged without validation".

## Fix

The guard must count a successful Quality run of **any** event (`workflow_dispatch`, `pull_request`, `push`) whose head/tree covers the merged tree — or at minimum add `pull_request`. The check is about *tree coverage by a green validation*, not about *who dispatched it*.

## Why not just silence the alarm

A too-narrow coverage check cries wolf on every conflict-rework merge (legs push → pull_request CI → merge): operators learn to ignore `[sm-guard]` alarms, and the one real unvalidated merge drowns in false positives.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Replaying the gh-1033 inputs (merged tree `89755209ac7d`, green pull_request run 39126212895 on head 32f43df1) yields NO alarm.
- [ ] A merge whose tree has NO green run of any event still alarms (true positive preserved).
- [ ] Unit test: coverage probe accepts pull_request/push/workflow_dispatch green runs alike; rejects red/in-flight runs of any event.
